text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — P1: NCCL_COMM_CORRUPTION on cluster-prod-5. Affected jobs: run-abc123 (tp4), run-def456 (pipeline). Error spike 21:04:50 UTC. Pager -> @ryan. Link: https://incidents.redwood/5519998888

ryan: on it, taking pager. starting quick triage.

dmitri: saw a similar pattern last month — kv-cache eviction + node flip caused comm mismatch. worth checking kvcache churn.

ryan: pulling GPU and container logs now.

carla: docker ps on node-5-3 shows multiple restarts for run-abc123 task.

ryan: log snippet from runtime:
```
[21:05:12] E NCCL: comm 0x7f9c... - NCCL_COMM_CORRUPTION detected
[21:05:12] E CUDA: cudaLaunchKernel failed: unspecified launch failure (Xid=79)
[21:05:12] I runtime: communicator failed, scheduling restart
```

jin: can we route affected requests to fallback model-small-cpu while we stabilize? That reduces customer error rate quickly.

nina: support data: ~6% of hosted generation requests returning 500s between 21:04–21:16 UTC for customers on region-us-west-2. No broad data-plane outage, isolated to tp/pipeline jobs.

ryan: hypothesis: node-5-3 experienced an ephemeral node flip + aggressive kv-cache eviction -> communicator init raced with KV cache state -> NCCL ended up with corrupted ring -> Xid driver reset.

carla: ps+docker logs show k8s OOMKiller events around the same time: "Killed process 3241 (runtime) total-vm..."

ryan: mitigation plan: 1) cordon node-5-3 2) drain tp/pipeline pods 3) restart runtime on drained pods with kvcache disabled for tp jobs 4) bump runtime communicator retry to 3 and longer backoff 5) route traffic to fallback model. Doing steps 1-3 now.

ryan: kubectl cordon node-5-3 && kubectl drain node-5-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data

ops-bot: deploy-bot: cordon accepted, drain initiated. Drain ETA ~2m.

carla: drain logs: some pods took >30s to shutdown due to long checkpointing; forced delete on two pods.

dmitri: tracing nccl handshake shows failure during bootstrap when kv-cache eviction triggered a change in keyset. We should make KV cache eviction observable in the runtime logs.

ryan: temp config applied on affected nodes: runtime.kvcache.enabled=false for tp jobs; runtime.comm.retry=3; runtime.comm.backoff_ms=500. Restarting runtime containers.

carla: restarts finished, containers stable. No new Xid79 in the last 2m.

nina: customer impact update: error rate down to ~0.2% after reroute. Informing support to pause alerts for impacted customers.

jin: taking oncall handoff in 30m — I'll stay on the thread and monitor until SL. If anything new appears ping me.

ryan: short-term summary for postmortem: probable root cause = KV cache eviction racing with NCCL communicator init on memory-constrained node causing communicator corruption and driver reset. Mitigations performed: node cordoned+drained, disabled kvcache for tp workloads on node, increased communicator retry/backoff, routed traffic to fallback model.

dmitri: follow-ups: add kvcache eviction metric to ops dashboard, add a pre-check in runtime to prevent kvcache GC during NCCL init, and add a recovery path to re-init communicator without global job failure.

nina: I'll draft a customer-facing incident note in #support with ETA for a deeper postmortem.

ryan: assigning postmortem owners: ryan, dmitri. Will create postmortem ticket after handoff.

carla: :thumbsup: all quiet now, keeping monitoring on.

jin: acknowledged, will take point after handoff.

ops-bot: incident-bot: handoff scheduled to jin at 22:00 UTC.

ryan: final note before handoff — keeping node-5-3 cordoned until we confirm a safe kvcache GC strategy.

nina: thanks everyone. I'll update customers in 15m with current status and next steps. :white_check_mark:
